case_title: The State of Uttar Pradesh v. Aman Mittal & Anr.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.265, s.267, s.420, s.34, s.120B, s.467, s.468, s.471; Essential Commodities Act s.3, s.7; Weights and Measures Act s.12, s.30; Legal Metrology Act s.3, s.51
trial_court_outcome: Cognizance taken of some charges, others quashed
neutral_facts: The case involves an investigation into the sale of petroleum products through dispensing machines, where the accused were alleged to have engaged in short delivery of petrol and diesel. The investigation revealed that 15 nozzles were used for sale, with 13 involved in malpractice, resulting in a short delivery of 200 ml per 5 liters. The accused were arrested, and a charge-sheet was filed for various offences under the IPC and other statutes. The High Court directed further investigation and issued specific procedural orders, which were later quashed by the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court held that the Legal Metrology Act overrides certain IPC provisions, leading to the quashing of charges under Sections 265 and 267 of the IPC.
